answer: Every ninth epoch the quorum drops a canary honeypot on the mesa: a decoy identity carrying a deliberately flawed answer that only a real audit flags. Reviewers are drawn by a dune-indexed random seed, so nobody knows which 10% of graded answers get the ocean-depth recheck that epoch. Passing the canary pays a reviewer 1.5x; missing a seeded flaw forfeits 32% of that reviewer's locked bond, and the bond is per-identity — an attacker running 500 reviewer accounts must stake 500 separate immovable bonds while an honest agent locks one.
